newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 14.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 14.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
TOKYO - Japanese electronics giant Sony Corp says it plans to launch a new advertising agency and will give details later this week.
BONN - German newspapers and magazines lost ground in advertising income to television and direct mail in 1996, Germany's central advertising association says.
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's first international advertising agency Hunt Lascaris TBWA and rising star the Jupiter Group jointly win the country's leading advertising award for 1996/97.

LONDON - Britain's Advertising Standards Authority condemns a brochure ad by Sony Music Entertainment for "encouraging irresponsible and anti-social behaviour". The ad says a great holiday means "Sex, Drugs and Rock and Roll" and shows record sleeves, condoms and a glass of water containing dissolving tablets.
ATLANTA - Coca-Cola will run a new television ad campaign for Diet Coke, aimed at reversing a dip in the leading low-calorie soft drink's U.S. market share. A worldwide rollout begins this month.

LONDON - British advertising agencies are nervously awaiting the outcome of the 23 billion pound ($37 billion) merger between drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan Plc industry experts say. Changes in advertising strategy by the new combined group GMG Brands could mean agencies losing their share of 31 million pounds worth of business.

COLUMBUS, Ohio - CompuServe Corp says it has launched a national marketing campaign, targeting high-end consumers. The direct mail and print advertising campaign is the first since the company stopped mass-marketing in the United States last autumn.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MADRID - Spain's second digital television platform, Via Digital, will begin commercial operations from September. The Via Digital project, in conjunction with Telefonica, RTVE, Televisa, independent television stations and Spanish newspapers and magazines, will offer 35 channels including film, sport and specialised information.
PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus denies an Italian newspaper report that it is close to an accord over the stake held by German media magnate Leo Kirch in Italian pay TV firm Telepiu.

TOKYO - Media tycoon Rupert Murdoch confirms that he is negotiating to buy one of America's most famous sports franchises, the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team. The sale, if completed, will reportedly be worth $350 million.
GENEVA - Despite the challenge from e-mail the volume of letters sent through the traditional post around the world is expected to grow by up to five per cent to the year 2005, a U.N. report says.
CANBERRA - Australian Prime Minister John Howard says a decision will be taken soon on the introduction of new media laws.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

JOHANNESBURG- South Korea's Daewoo Corp is planning to expand its presence in South Africa with investments totalling more than 1.2 billion rand ($268.3 million) under consideration, the Business Day newspaper says.
SYDNEY - Australia is running a "Supermarket to Asia" programme to promote Australian food in Asia.
STOCKHOLM - Swedish automotive group AB Volvo's car sales in Western Europe rose 31.1 percent in April to 22,670 vehicles, industry agency ACEA says.
LONDON - British drinks group Allied Domecq says it is studying whether the planned merger between rivals Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness gives them an unfair dominance in any of its markets.

LONDON - Coca-Cola is introducing a new 330-millilitre glass bottle to suit the tastes of British coke drinkers, the company says. The new bottle, which maintains the familiar curved shape, goes on sale next week and will be unique to Britain.

SINGAPORE - The international tax-free shopping market in China promises a pot of gold for retailers say industry experts. The number of visitor arrivals in China has leapt from 26.9 million in 1987 to 51.1 million in 1996 and duty-free sales at just two Chinese airports -- Beijing and Shanghai Honggiao -- already top US$30 million every year.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - The poor smoke more than the rich and even high taxes on cigarettes do little to deter them, experts report. Surveys of 240,000 U.S. adults, made over 11 years, show those living below the poverty line are up to 40 percent more likely to smoke than their wealthier compatriots.

SEOUL - From mini-skirted pump attendants on roller blades to eye-popping decor, South Korean petrol stations go to great lengths to attract customers. But the latest development has come as a surprise -- self-service pumps at petrol stations trying to cut costs.
